# Native PRJ common return

Six actual Sonnet 18.53 Lite CKT cases contain implicit ground, explicit node0,
common node7 with a resistor toground, an external return port, two blocks
sharing node7, and two blocks sharing an external return. All18 complete-S
matrices pass the unchanged1e-10 gate against an independent signed-incidence
nodal oracle (maximum5.63e-13). Final actual run: native_prj_common_return_77wGmW;
its 66 assertions passed. Native raw-log/output/reference guards are retained.

The saved GUI assigns REF to node7, adding that node immediately before the
project filename. Installed NetProjectWin primary explicitly permits this
assignment. The trailing0/1 PRJ field is unchanged by the implementation; its
meaning remains separately unresolved. It is not identified as a child type.

Captured original production methods reject valid records before model callbacks.
The isolated overlay preserves raw sources and uses explicit (pin,return) MNA
terminal pairs. Public native comparisons, return KCL, null common mode,
calibrated geometry voltage/current projection, recursive bounded SPROJ staging,
stale dependency ownership and transactional resource checks are separate tests.
The calibrated geometry test supplies explicit launch chains; it does not claim
native SOC extraction or a general automatic geometry child adapter.

Original failed probes remain: first child and parent FILEOUT paths collided and
the output-vs-log guard rejected; second used a vector norm on rounded external
text for common-mode cancellation; third omitted SID continuation rows. Final
native null-mode assertions use full-precision SID after the output guard. The
first overlay loaded physical test correctly rejected an unaligned coarser grid;
the final uses the original32x40 grid. One final overlay attempt raced the
coordinated ProjectFiles integration; captured original methods were subsequently
restored only in the isolated Julia process. No archived report credits a live
source hash for a different captured source.

Actual SMD SPROJ analysis remains independently Lite license-blocked. Loaded
physical regressions test our circuit/EM composition, not licensed native SMD
acceptance, continuum convergence, measured devices or general RFIC parity.
